paper_title: Limits on new long range nuclear spin-dependent forces set with a K-3He co-magnetometer
coupling_convention: dimensionless g_an, converted from the paper's (g_p^n)^2/(4pi) < 5.8e-10 via g = sqrt(4*pi*5.8e-10)
notes: K-3He co-magnetometer search for anomalous neutron spin-dependent forces from a 3He spin source (Vasilakis et al., Princeton, 2008/2009). The paper's Fig. 4 shows (g_p^n)^2/4pi vs boson mass from ~1e-7 meV to 1 meV, but the only explicit numerical value in text is the massless-boson limit (g_p^n)^2/4pi < 5.8e-10 (a factor 500 better than the 3He-129Xe maser). This flat bound is encoded as a horizontal line up to m ~ hbar*c/(50 cm) ~ 4e-7 eV, where the Yukawa suppression from the 48.7 cm source-detector distance sets in; above this the actual limit weakens (rises), so the full mass-dependent curve from Fig. 4 is not captured. This is a fifth-force-type laboratory limit, NOT a dark matter search, so no local DM density is assumed. Note: the quoted bound is a 1-sigma (~68% CL) limit per the paper; 0.90 is the closest allowed enum value.
